meaning:
προ-γινώσκω
[in LXX: Wis.6:13 8:8 18:6 * ;]
to know beforehand, foreknow: 2Pe.3:17; with accusative of person(s), Act.26:5; of the Divine foreknowledge, Rom.8:29 11:2, 1Pe.1:20.†
(AS)

renderings.kjv: eeing ye know these things before

elsewhere.note: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers.
who was foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in this last age for your sake,
You therefore, beloved, knowing these things beforehand, beware, lest being carried away with the error of the wicked, you fall from your own steadfastness.
